column2: Run the data centre on clean, renewable energy.
column3: Use cooling systems that recycle their own water, instead of taking water the town needs.
column4: Protect local plants and animals — including species already at risk of dying out — and the places they live.
column5: Have an independent group check and publish how much pollution and noise the site produces, and what it does to people's health.
column6: Create long-term local jobs and training — not just short-term work during construction.
column7: Don't let this damage the tourism and farming we already have — protect the industries that are already here.
column8: Reuse the data centre's waste heat for local benefit — for example, to heat greenhouses for local farms.
column9: Share some of the data centre's computing power with schools, researchers and businesses — to grow a tech and research hub with local jobs and training that come with it.
column10: Make sure any benefit is ongoing, not a single payment — and give the community a real, binding say in how it's spent.
column11: Instead of deciding case by case, put benefit money straight into fixing rundown local infrastructure and restoring nature.
column12: Give Traditional Custodians a real, paid role in decisions about this project — not just a token consultation.
column13: Set rules for how the data centre looks and where it's built, to protect the Highlands' rural character.
column14: Demand at least six weeks to respond to any proposal — time to get organised, understand it, and put in a real submission.
